subject: Re: Pilot model recommendations + latency slate for ClarityTech
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Kapoor <sana@claritytech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-08T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot model recommendations + latency slate for ClarityTech

Hi Sana —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard
- Primary use case: customer support triage + short-form summary generation from ticket text (~120 tokens output).
- Target latency: p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 260 ms under bursty traffic (40 rps peak for initial pilot).
- Quality expectation: F1-style label > 0.78 on your annotated validation set for triage classification; summaries should match customer-rated usefulness > 4/5 in initial QA.

Recommended slate (Redwood-verified profiles attached)
1) rw-small-v2-int8 (recommended default) — best cost/latency for shorter sequences. Verified throughput: 320 TPS on a single A10G-equivalent pod; median latency 48 ms, p95 115 ms, p99 240 ms (see attached CSV).
2) rw-medium-v1-fp16 — higher quality option, throughput 140 TPS, median 82 ms, p95 160 ms, p99 290 ms.
3) rw-small-qa-specialized (quantized) — for cases where classification precision matters; slightly higher p99 but better calibrated outputs.

What I attached / links
- redwood-verified-bench-clarity-20281008.csv (per-model TPS and latency percentiles measured using your sample prompt mixes)
- clarity-prompt-set-v1.txt (the prompt templates we used for benchmarking + the evaluation prompts)
- Google Drive folder with traces and raw perf artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBenchmarks

Immediate next steps
- If you agree with the slate, we’ll provision a 2-week pilot (reserved burst capacity) using rw-small-v2-int8 for the initial run and rw-medium-v1-fp16 as fallback.
- Laura will share a pilot SOW draft and the DocuSign link for the pilot contract.
- Please loop in procurement (procurement@claritytech.com) with target PO timing.

Questions for you
- Do you want us to prioritize p99 over cost in the pilot, or run the default cost-aware profile first?
- Any constraints on data residency I should be aware of for logs/artifacts?

Thanks — I’ve copied Laura and Dylan on the plan. If that looks good I’ll schedule the pilot kickoff for next Tuesday.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0219

Thanks Aditya — helpful writeup and the numbers look promising. A couple quick clarifications: 

- On the rw-small-v2-int8 numbers, can you confirm the test sequence distribution? We typically have 60% short (<=64 tokens) and 40% medium (65-256 tokens) during business hours. Will that materially change the p99?
- For the pilot SOW, we prefer a canary-based rollout so customer-facing flows use fallback only on degradation. Can your runtime do autoswitching based on p95 breaches?

Procurement is cc’d. We’re OK proceeding with the two-model slate so long as we can confirm the p99 under our sequence mix and add a regression guardrail for quality (we’ll provide an initial labeled set for evaluation).

Would it be possible to get an annotated run (trace-level latencies + example outputs) from the rw-small-v2-int8 run you attached? That would help our infra folks validate SLA assumptions.

— Sana
Head of Product, ClarityTech
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

On Mon, Oct 8, 2028 at 6:03 PM, Sana Kapoor <sana@claritytech.com> wrote:
> Thanks Aditya — helpful writeup and the numbers look promising. A couple quick clarifications: 
> 
> - On the rw-small-v2-int8 numbers, can you confirm the test sequence distribution? We typically have 60% short (<=64 tokens) and 40% medium (65-256 tokens) during business hours. Will that materially change the p99?

Hi Sana —

Good question. The CSV we attached contains separate rows for our short/medium/long mixes. For the exact 60/40 short-to-medium split you described, we re-ran the microbench and observed: median 54 ms, p95 128 ms, p99 265 ms on an A10G-equivalent pod (single replica). The p99 increases modestly because medium requests incur higher KV cache pressure; however, with Redwood's adaptive batching and prefix caching the observed production p99 improves by ~8-12% compared to raw single-request runs.

Regarding canary autoswitching: yes — our routing policies support rule-based failover (p95 breach or error rate threshold) and automatic routing to the fallback model (rw-medium-v1-fp16). We can set the policy to only switch for a worker pool serving your customer-facing endpoint and keep internal QA traffic on the trial model.

About annotated traces: attached to this message is a small trace pack (in the Drive folder) with per-request latencies and example outputs we redacted for customer PII. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleBenchmarks (same folder). I also dropped a short README in the folder explaining columns in the CSV.

Regression guardrail suggestion:
- Baseline classification F1 and summary ROUGE-L on your labeled eval set (we’ll import your labels into the Redwood eval harness).
- Set an automatic rollback trigger if F1 drops > 3 points vs baseline during pilot sampling, or if semantic-quality scores fall 10% vs baseline on a 48-hour rolling window.

We’ll include those in the pilot SOW. Monica, can you attach the SOW draft and DocuSign link?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
GM, Discovery & Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Sana / procurement team —

Great — thanks for confirming. Quick execution plan and dates: 

1) Pilot SOW & signature: Monica has uploaded the SOW to DocuSign (link below). Please review; we can accept signatures from a delegated PO approver. Target: signature by 2028-10-11.
   - DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/templates/clarity-pilot-sow
2) Tech kickoff & canary config: 2028-10-16 (30 min). Redwood runtime will configure canary policy: p95 threshold 140 ms (auto-fallback), error rate threshold 1.5%.
3) Pilot run (2 weeks): 2028-10-17 to 2028-10-31. We’ll run rw-small-v2-int8 primary, rw-medium-v1-fp16 fallback.
4) Evaluation checkpoint: 2028-10-25 (we’ll run the labeled eval and deliver the quality report).

Deliverables during pilot:
- Daily perf snapshot (TPS, median, p95, p99) and example outputs (5 anonymized).
- Regression guardrail alerts configured into your Slack channel (or webhook).
- Post-pilot recommendation: produce the production runbook with cost estimates and SLOs.

Procurement — please confirm preferred billing contact and whether a PO will arrive prior to signature. If you prefer, I can share a short billing worksheet.

Notes on the bench numbers and what to expect at scale:
- The attached CSV includes raw traces and the aggregated latencies. Our verified number for rw-small-v2-int8 under your 60/40 mix (single-replica A10G) is p99 265 ms; deploying a two-replica pool with burst scaling reduces observed p99 to ~200–220 ms for identical load patterns. We’ll size accordingly once we have a 48-hour traffic sample.

If that timeline looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the kickoff.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
